description: Polls a Slack channel and launches a chat-agent asset for a mention, a DM, or a reply in an already-answered thread -- identifiers only in run tags, never the message text.

slack_channel_id.label: Slack Channel Id
slack_channel_id.description: Channel ID to poll (e.g. 'C0123ABCDEF' or a DM's 'D0123ABCDEF') -- NOT a '#channel-name'; conversations.history requires the real id.

asset_selection.label: Asset Selection
asset_selection.description: The agent asset (and anything downstream, e.g. a slack_reply asset) to materialize when a message matches: explicit key list, the Dagster selection DSL (tag:/group:/kind:/boolean composition), '*', or a bare fnmatch glob -- resolved against sibling assets in the same defs folder.

slack_bot_token_env_var.label: Slack Bot Token Env Var
slack_bot_token_env_var.description: Env var holding the bot's 'xoxb-...' token. Needs channels:history (or groups:history) + chat:write + reactions:write + users:read.email scopes.

bot_user_id.label: Bot User Id
bot_user_id.description: This bot's own Slack user id, for mention-detection ('<@BOT_ID>' in a message) and self-exclusion. Auto-discovered via auth.test if unset -- set explicitly only to skip that one extra API call per tick.

trigger_mode.label: Trigger Mode
trigger_mode.description: 'mention' (default): only a message that @-mentions the bot starts a NEW conversation (a reply in an already-tracked thread still matches regardless of mode -- see follow_up_threads). 'dm' and 'all' both match every new root message unconditionally and are functionally identical; 'dm' exists as a separate name purely so a DM channel's config reads as a DM, not as 'answer literally everything' by accident. Never use 'all'/'dm' on a busy shared channel -- the bot would answer every single message in it.

follow_up_threads.label: Follow Up Threads
follow_up_threads.description: Also launch a run for a NEW REPLY in a thread this sensor has already launched a run for -- not gated by trigger_mode, so once a thread is tracked, every new reply in it triggers another run, not just ones that re-mention the bot. Costs one extra conversations.replies call per tracked thread per tick (see known_threads_limit) -- set false for a channel with many concurrent long-lived threads.

known_threads_limit.label: Known Threads Limit
known_threads_limit.description: Most-recently-active threads to keep polling for follow-ups. Bounds both cursor size and the extra conversations.replies calls follow_up_threads costs per tick. Lowered from an earlier default of 200 -- that many conversations.replies calls every tick exhausted a real workspace's Slack quota. See also follow_up_window_minutes, a second, time-based bound on the same set.

resolve_requester_email.label: Resolve Requester Email
resolve_requester_email.description: Resolve the message sender's Slack user id to an email address (needs users:read.email) before setting the slack/user tag -- most owners: checks downstream (e.g. dagster_workflow_tools' launch_job) use emails, not Slack user ids. When false, slack/user carries the raw Slack user id instead.

messages_per_poll.label: Messages Per Poll
messages_per_poll.description: Root messages to request per Slack page (Slack's own recommended max is 200).

max_pages_per_poll.label: Max Pages Per Poll
max_pages_per_poll.description: Follow at most this many pagination cursors per poll, for both new-root-message and (per-thread) new-reply polling.

process_backlog_on_first_run.label: Process Backlog On First Run
process_backlog_on_first_run.description: If false (default), the first-ever tick seeds the cursor to 'now' and processes nothing -- activating this sensor never answers a channel's past history.

post_acknowledgement.label: Post Acknowledgement
post_acknowledgement.description: React to a matched message immediately (acknowledgement_reaction) so the sender sees it was received before the agent run even starts.

acknowledgement_reaction.label: Acknowledgement Reaction
acknowledgement_reaction.description: Reaction name for post_acknowledgement (one of Slack's built-in emoji names, e.g. 'eyes', 'thinking_face').

set_isolation_disabled_tag.label: Set Isolation Disabled Tag
set_isolation_disabled_tag.description: Tag every RunRequest dagster/isolation: disabled, so the run starts in-process on the code location server instead of spinning up an isolated container (which can take up to 3 minutes on Dagster+ -- far too slow for chat). Needs non_isolated_runs enabled on the deployment, and a sensible max_concurrent_non_isolated_runs (default 1 on Dagster+ -- a second concurrent question falls back to a slow isolated run, not a queue, if you don't raise it). See the README's 'Isolation' section -- Dagster's own docs are inconsistent about whether this is on by default.

minimum_interval_seconds.label: Minimum Interval Seconds
minimum_interval_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between sensor evaluations. Chat latency is roughly this plus the run-queue dequeue time plus the LLM call -- keep this low.

default_status.label: Default Status
default_status.description: 'RUNNING' or 'STOPPED' -- initial status of the sensor.

use_in_process_executor.label: Use In Process Executor
use_in_process_executor.description: Tag every RunRequest with run_config={'execution': {'config': {'in_process': {}}}}, so the agent asset and its downstream slack_reply asset run as plain function calls in one step-process instead of each spawning its own multiprocess-executor subprocess -- real subprocess spawn time otherwise adds up on top of set_isolation_disabled_tag's own container-startup savings. Requires the code location that owns these assets not to set a non-default executor itself (e.g. k8s_job_executor/celery_executor/docker_executor) -- if it does, this run_config key is rejected by that executor's own config schema and the run fails with a RunConfigValidationInvalid error. Set false to leave execution untouched.

placeholder_text.label: Placeholder Text
placeholder_text.description: If set, post this text as a new thread reply right after acknowledging a matched message, and tag the run slack/placeholder_ts with that reply's own ts. slack_reply then updates THIS message with the final answer (chat.update) instead of posting a new one, and its failure_watcher updates it with the error -- so a 20-30s wait shows 'Looking into it…' (or whatever text you set) instead of nothing. Needs chat:write (already required). Leave unset (default) to skip this -- slack_reply just posts new replies, as before. Checked against Slack's own docs, not assumed: the newer agents.sessions.setStatus DOES work in regular channel threads (not just the AI-assistant pane the older assistant.threads.setStatus is scoped to), but it has no free-text status (an enum: active/processing/suspended/closed) and needs the Agents feature enabled on the workspace (feature_disabled error otherwise) -- this placeholder message is what actually shows free text like 'Looking into it…' in an ordinary channel, everywhere, with no feature flag.

follow_up_window_minutes.label: Follow Up Window Minutes
follow_up_window_minutes.description: Only poll a tracked thread for follow-ups if its last-seen reply was within this many minutes -- a second bound alongside known_threads_limit's count cap, so a long-dormant thread doesn't keep costing a conversations.replies call every tick forever. Unset: no time bound, only known_threads_limit's count cap applies.

skip_in_branch_deployments.label: Skip In Branch Deployments
skip_in_branch_deployments.description: Skip every tick while running inside a Dagster+ branch deployment (DAGSTER_CLOUD_IS_BRANCH_DEPLOYMENT=1). A branch deployment runs its own copy of every sensor alongside the full deployment's -- without this, a branch deployment double-acknowledges the same message and double-launches a run for it.
